source_title: Aon Reports Third-Quarter 2026 Results - PR Newswire
source_excerpt:
DUBLIN , Oct. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Aon plc (NYSE: AON ) today reported results for the three months ended September 30, 2026.
Aon delivered another quarter of strong performance, including 3% total revenue growth, 6% organic revenue growth and EPS growth. Our results showcased broad-based strength across solution lines, with organic revenue growth of 7% in Commercial Risk, 7% in Reinsurance, 6% in Health and 4% in Wealth
Our disciplined capital allocation framework is supported by strong free cash flow generation. We expect the USI Acquisition to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, and will prioritize debt repayment with a path towards deleveraging to our 2.8x-3.0x objective in approximately 24 months
We enter the fourth quarter with significant momentum, reinforcing our confidence in our ability to deliver strong financial performance for full-year 2026
(millions, except percentages and per share data)
"Our Aon United strategy continues to advance and differentiate our platform for clients," said Greg Case, president and CEO. "As we progress through the final year of our 3x3 Plan, our investments in AI-enabled analytics, innovative capabilities and capital solutions, and leading experts are helping clients address their risks, build resilience and drive better outcomes. At the same time, we are strengthening our context advantage and expanding our ability to serve clients across a broader market through the announced acquisition of USI, while creating new opportunities through greater access to both traditional and alternative sources of capital."
Case added: "The impact of this strategy is further demonstrated by our strong third-quarter results with 6% organic revenue growth, 70 basis points of adjusted margin expansion and 10% adjusted EPS growth. We enter the fourth quarter with significant momentum, reinforcing confidence in our ongoing ability to deliver sustained, differentiated performance."
Net income attributable to Aon shareholders in the third quarter increased 6%, to $2.23 per share on a diluted basis, compared to $2.11 per share on a diluted basis, in the prior-year period. Adjusted net income per share attributable to Aon shareholders increased 10% to $3.36 on a diluted basis, including a $0.02 favorable impact if prior-year period results were translated at current-period foreign exchange rates ("foreign currency translation"), compared to $3.05 in the prior-year period. Certain items that impacted third-quarter results and comparisons with the prior-year period are detailed in "Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Measures - Operating Income and Operating Margin (Unaudited)" and "Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Measures - Diluted Earnings Per Share (Unaudited)" beginning on page 11 of this press release.
Total revenue in the third quarter increased 3% to $4.1 billion compared to the prior-year period, reflecting 6% organic revenue growth, partially offset by a 3% unfavorable impact primarily from divestitures. Risk Capital revenue increased $157 million, or 6%, to $2.7 billion and Human Capital revenue decreased $54 million, or 4%, to $1.4 billion.
Total operating expenses in the third quarter increased 3% to $3.3 billion compared to the prior-year period due primarily to an increase in expense associated with 6% organic revenue growth, investments in long-term growth, and an increase in Accelerating Aon United Program expenses, partially offset by lower expenses associated with the sale of the NFP Wealth business and $20 million of net restructuring savings. Risk Capital operating expenses increased $134 million, or 7%, and Human Capital operating expenses decreased $68 million, or 6%.
Foreign currency translation had a $0.02 favorable impact on both diluted EPS and adjusted EPS in the third quarter. If currency were to remain stable at today's rates, the Company would expect a de minimis impact on adjusted EPS in the fourth quarter of 2026 and a favorable impact on adjusted EPS of approximately $0.42 per share for the full year 2026.
Effective tax rate was 20.6% in the third quarter compared to 21.3% in the prior-year period. After adjusting to exclude the applicable tax impact associated with certain non-GAAP adjustments, the adjusted effective tax rate for the third quarter of 2026 was 20.2% compared to 19.2% in the prior-year period. The primary drivers of the change in the effective tax rate were changes to the geographical distribution of income and a greater net unfavorable impact from discrete items. The primary drivers of the change in the adjusted effective tax rate were changes to the geographical distribution of income and a net unfavorable impact from discrete items.
Weighted average diluted shares outstanding decreased to 213.0 million in the third quarter compared to 216.7 million in the prior-year period. The Company did not repurchase any shares in the third quarter. As of September 30, 2026, the Company had approximately $7.7 billion of remaining authorization under its share repurchase program.
Cash flows provided by operations for the first nine months of 2026 increased $93 million, or 4%, to $2.2 billion compared to the prior-year period, as strong adjusted operating income growth offset the impact of working capital and USI-related transaction costs.
Free cash flow , defined as cash flow from operations less capital expenditures, increased 3%, to $1.9 billion for the first nine months of 2026 compared to the prior-year period, reflecting an increase in cash flows provided by operations, partially offset by a $45 million increase in capital expenditures.
The third-quarter revenue reviews provided below include supplemental information related to organic revenue growth, which is a non-GAAP measure that is described in detail in "Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Measures - Organic Revenue Growth and Free Cash Flow" on page 10 of this press release.
Total revenue increased $104 million, or 3%, compared to the prior-year period, reflecting 6% organic revenue growth, driven by net new business and ongoing strong retention, partially offset by a 3% unfavorable impact primarily from divestitures largely due to the sales of the NFP Wealth business and Stroz Friedberg. Risk Capital revenue increased $157 million, or 6%, and Human Capital revenue decreased $54 million, or 4%.
Commercial Risk Solutions Organic revenue growth of 7% reflects strong growth in North America and EMEA, driven by net new business and ongoing strong retention. Net market impact was slightly positive. Within North America, performance was highlighted by strong growth in M&A services and U.S. core P&C, and growth in construction.
Reinsurance Solutions Organic revenue growth of 7% reflects strong growth in treaty placements, driven by net new business and strong retention, and a favorable impact from the reversal of the constraint applied against prior period revenue. Net market impact was unfavorable in the quarter.
Health Solutions Organic revenue growth of 6% reflects strong growth in core health and benefits, including particular strength internationally, driven by net new business and ongoing strong retention, as well as growth in Talent Solutions driven by talent analytics. Net market impact was modestly positive.
Wealth Solutions Organic revenue growth of 4% reflects strong growth in Retirement, driven by continued demand for advisory work in the UK and EMEA related to the ongoing impact of regulatory change.
Amortization and impairment of intangible assets
Compensation and benefits expense increased $16 million, or 1%, compared to the prior-year period, due primarily to higher expenses associated with 6% organic revenue growth and investments in long-term growth, partially offset by lower expenses from the sale of the NFP Wealth business and savings from Accelerating Aon United restructuring actions.
Information technology expense increased $16 million, or 11%, compared to the prior-year period, due primarily to Aon Business Services investments in ongoing technology initiatives.
Premises expense decreased $2 million, or 2%, compared to the prior-year period, as we continued to optimize our real estate footprint and recognize savings from Accelerating Aon United restructuring actions.
Depreciation of fixed assets increased $2 million, or 4%, compared to the prior-year period.
Amortization and impairment of intangible assets decreased $18 million, or 9%, compared to the prior-year period, due primarily to the decrease in intangible assets associated with the sale of the NFP Wealth business.
Other general expense increased $36 million, or 8%, compared to the prior-year period, due primarily to a recovery in the prior-year period associated with a legal settlement as well as USI-related transaction costs.
Accelerating Aon United Restructuring Program expense increased $61 million, or 191%, compared to the prior-year period, due primarily to costs related to workforce optimization.
Certain noteworthy items impacted adjusted operating income and adjusted operating margin in the third quarters of 2026 and 2025, which are also described in detail in "Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Measures - Operating Income and Operating Margin (Unaudited)" and "Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Measures - Diluted Earnings Per Share (Unaudited)" on page 11 of this press release.
Operating income decreased $7 million, or 1%, and operating margin decreased 70 basis points to 19.7%, each compared to the prior-year period. Adjusted operating income increased $55 million, or 5%, and adjusted operating margin increased 70 basis points to 27.0%, each compared to the prior-year period. The increase in adjusted operating income reflects organic revenue growth, scale improvements in ABS and net restructuring savings, partially offset by investments for growth.
Interest income increased $24 million compared to the prior-year period, primarily reflecting higher cash balances as a result of the net proceeds raised from debt issuance. Interest expense was flat compared to the prior-year period. Lower average debt balances during much of the quarter were offset by interest expense associated with debt issued near the end of the quarter to fund the USI Acquisition.
Other expense and adjusted other expense were $15 million compared to $13 million in the prior-year period, primarily due to the unfavorable impact of exchange rates on the remeasurement of assets and liabilities in non-functional currencies.
Net income attributable to Aon shareholders increased 4% to $476 million compared to $458 million in the prior-year period. Adjusted net income attributable to Aon shareholders increased 8% to $715 million compared to $660 million in the prior-year period.
Conference Call, Presentation Slides, and Webcast Details
The Company will host a conference call on Wednesday, October 28, 2026 at 8:30 a.m., eastern time. Interested parties can listen to the conference call via a live audio webcast and view the presentation slides at ir.aon.com.

Explanation of Non-GAAP Measures This communication includes supplemental information not calculated in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States ("U.S. GAAP"), including organic revenue growth, free cash flow, adjusted operating income, adjusted operating margin, adjusted net income, adjusted net income attributable to Aon shareholders, adjusted diluted net income per share ("EPS"), adjusted effective tax rate, adjusted other income (expense), adjusted income tax expense, leverage ratio, and adjusted income before income taxes that exclude the effects of intangible asset amortization and impairment, Accelerating Aon United Program expenses, contingent consideration, NFP integration costs, USI transaction costs, certain pension settlements, capital expenditures, and certain other noteworthy items that affected results for the comparable periods. Organic revenue growth includes the impact of intercompany activity and excludes foreign exchange rate changes, acquisitions (provided that organic revenue growth includes organic growth of an acquired business as calculated assuming that the acquired business was part of the combined company for the same proportion of the relevant prior-year period), divestitures (including held for sale disposal groups, if any, which are adjusted from organic revenue growth upon classification as held-for-sale), transfers between revenue lines, fiduciary investment income, and gains or losses on derivatives accounted for as hedges. Currency impact represents the effect on prior-year period results if they were translated at current-period foreign exchange rates. Reconciliations to the closest U.S. GAAP measure for each non-GAAP measure presented in this communication are provided in the attached appendices. Supplemental organic revenue growth information and additional measures that exclude the effects of certain items noted above do not affect net income or any other U.S. GAAP reported amounts. Free cash flow is cash flows from operating activity less capital expenditures. The adjusted effective tax rate excludes the applicable tax impact associated with adjustments previously described, generally at the estimated annual effective tax rate or jurisdictional rate, where appropriate. Beginning in the third quarter of 2024, the adjusted effective tax rate also excludes interest accruals for income tax reserves related to the termination fee payment made in connection with the Company's terminated proposed combination with Willis Towers Watson. Leverage ratio is calculated by dividing total debt by trailing 12-month EBITDA. EBITDA is net income minus the impact of interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, and the non-recurring gain from the sale of the substantial majority of NFP's Wealth business. Management believes that these measures are important to make meaningful period-to-period comparisons and that this supplemental information is helpful to investors. Management also uses certain of these measures to assess operating performance and performance for compensation. Non-GAAP measures should be viewed in addition to, not in lieu of, Aon's Consolidated Financial Statements. Industry peers provide similar supplemental information regarding their performance, although they may not make identical adjustments.
